narrative.overview:
PolAI is a calm, exact writing instrument. The source text is the interface, not content placed inside an ornamental application shell. The visual system borrows the discipline of an archival condition report: matte inspection paper, compact labels, hairline rules, and numbered observations that appear only where attention is required.

The interface stays neutral and nonpartisan. Mineral green carries actions and completion; mint and amber distinguish linked findings without implying political sides or severity. Space, scale, and alignment create hierarchy before containers or decoration do.
keyCharacteristics: Continuous, editor-first workspace with a narrow evidence rail.
Matte paper surfaces separated by hairline rules, with no elevation.
System sans typography that shifts from generous reading copy to compact inspection labels.
Exact source spans linked to numbered findings by matching mint or amber treatments.
Direct, neutral controls that keep every revision under the writer's control.

rules.name: The Nonpartisan Color Rule
rules.body: Color may link evidence, signal interaction state, or report system status; it must never encode a political side.

rules.name: The Matched Evidence Rule
rules.body: Every marked source span and its corresponding finding use the same fill and edge treatment, with explicit numbering and labels as non-color cues.

rules.name: The Paper Restraint Rule
rules.body: Large surfaces stay within the paper neutrals. Accent fills belong to compact evidence and state treatments.

rules.name: The Source Leads Rule
rules.body: Source prose receives the largest sustained reading treatment; analysis copy never competes with it.

rules.name: The Instrument Label Rule
rules.body: Uppercase labels identify regions and states, not marketing messages or long sentences.

rules.name: The Continuous Workspace Rule
rules.body: Desktop editor and analysis regions share one viewport-height field, one seam, and aligned headers.

rules.name: The Task-Order Rule
rules.body: Compact layouts preserve the workflow order: write, act, then review.

rules.name: The Flat Inspection Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Use rules, tone, and active outlines—not drop shadows—to establish structure.

rules.name: The Exception Shape Rule
rules.body: Rounded silhouettes must explain status, index, or compact interaction; they are not decorative containers.

dos: Do keep source text visually dominant and editable throughout review.
Do connect every finding to its exact phrase with matched tone, edge, number, and label.
Do use paper tone, hairline rules, and spacing to organize the workspace.
Do keep explanations and suggested neutral wording compact, direct, and scannable.
Do preserve visible focus, sufficient contrast, semantic regions, and reduced-motion-safe behavior.
donts: Don't introduce giant cards, floating dashboard panels, gradients, gauges, or decorative imagery.
Don't use red/blue, left/right, or any partisan color code for findings.
Don't apply excessive rounding; square regions and compact 2-3px controls are the default.
Don't add shadows for elevation or decoration.
Don't let analysis chrome, percentages, or status treatments compete with the source text.
